skill.name: linear
skill.description: Manage Linear issues, projects, documents, and team workflows through the Linear MCP server.
skill.summary: Plan, inspect, and update Linear work with structured, permission-aware workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Eleven static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, tool names, or unrelated prose. Official Linear connections are intended, but the WSL fallback executes an unpinned npm package and creates a high supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: The Windows and WSL fallback runs an unpinned mcp-remote package with npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version and require user confirmation before downloading or executing it.

static_findings.snippet: - Set `[features] rmcp_client = true` in `config.toml` **or** run `codex --enable rmcp_client`
- Leverage context: reference prior issues in new requests.
- Tool Calling Errors: Confirm the model supports multiple tool calls, provide all required fields,
- Break large updates into smaller batches to avoid rate limits; cache or reuse filters when listing

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 27 is a Markdown-formatted Codex setup command with fixed arguments. Backticks delimit inline code and do not execute Ruby or shell code.
Line 29 uses Markdown backticks to identify a configuration setting and a fixed CLI option. The file contains prose, not an execution mechanism.
Line 31 presents a fixed OAuth login command as inline Markdown. No backtick evaluation or user-controlled shell construction exists.
Line 36 starts a fenced JSON example. The fence is documentation syntax and cannot execute a shell command.
Line 38 closes a fenced JSON example. The backticks are Markdown structure, not executable syntax.
Line 57 formats Linear MCP tool names as inline code. It contains no shell command or dynamic execution.
Line 59 lists project and team tool identifiers in Markdown. These names are not shell expressions.
Line 61 lists documentation and collaboration tool identifiers. Markdown backticks only format the names.
Line 79 advises referencing prior issues. It contains no Python library, HTTP request, or network code.
Line 85 contains troubleshooting prose about tool calls. No Python HTTP library or direct request appears.
Line 27 directs Codex to connect to the fixed Linear MCP endpoint. This intended integration crosses a network trust boundary and may transmit authorized workspace data.
Line 37 configures mcp-remote to connect to Linear's fixed SSE endpoint. The official destination is expected, but the connection still exposes authorized data to an external service.
Line 80 recommends smaller batches and reused filters to respect rate limits. It does not inspect the host system or collect system information.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution in WSL Setup
semantic_findings.description: The fallback runs npx -y mcp-remote without a version pin, allowing registry changes or package compromise to execute code without an install prompt.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 37 explicitly combines npx, automatic confirmation, and an unversioned package name. This is a direct and well-established package supply-chain exposure.

content.value_statement: Linear work becomes difficult to coordinate across issues, projects, documents, and teams. This skill provides structured MCP workflows for reviewing and updating that work.
actual_capabilities: List, inspect, create, and update Linear issues.
List, inspect, create, and update Linear projects.
Review teams, users, labels, statuses, and cycles.
Search documents and read or create issue comments.
Guide OAuth setup for the Linear MCP server.
Organize sprint planning, triage, workload, and release workflows.
limitations: Requires a connected Linear MCP server and successful OAuth access.
Operations remain limited by the user's Linear workspace permissions.
The listed tools do not support deleting records or creating cycles.
Bulk operations remain subject to Linear API rate limits.

use_cases.title: Triage Product Bugs
use_cases.description: Review urgent bugs, rank impact, and update selected issues after confirming team scope.

use_cases.title: Plan a Release
use_cases.description: Create a release project, organize milestones, and generate scoped issues with assignments.

use_cases.title: Audit Documentation
use_cases.description: Search existing documentation and create issues for missing, outdated, or unclear content.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: List my open issues for team [team], group them by priority, and summarize blocked items without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Critical Bugs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review critical bugs in [team], rank them by user impact, recommend owners, and wait for confirmation before updates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Release Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release plan for [version] with milestones, required issues, estimates, and assignments after showing the proposed structure.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Cross-Project Blockers
prompt_templates.prompt: Find blocked issues across [projects], trace dependencies, identify missing links, and propose a sequenced resolution plan before applying changes.

output_examples.input: Show my open issues for the Platform team.
output: LIN-142 is blocked by an unresolved authentication dependency.
Two medium-priority issues have no current assignee.

output_examples.input: Prepare a documentation audit for API authentication.
output: Found gaps in token rotation and error handling guidance.
Prepared two documentation issues for review before creation.

output_examples.input: Balance active work across the Mobile team.
output: One assignee has substantially more active issues than the team average.
Suggested moving two unstarted issues to available team members.
No assignments were changed without confirmation.

best_practices: Confirm the target workspace, team, project, and identifiers before making changes.
Read existing records first, then explain proposed updates before applying them.
Use focused filters and small batches to reduce rate-limit and scope errors.
anti_patterns: Do not update large issue sets without reviewing the selected records.
Do not assume team keys, project identifiers, priorities, or due dates.
Do not retry authentication failures without checking access and OAuth status.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Linear issues, projects, documents, comments, labels, teams, users, statuses, and cycle information.

faq.question: Does it require a Linear account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need Linear workspace access and OAuth authorization for the Linear MCP server.

faq.question: Can it make changes automatically?
faq.answer: It can create or update supported records when requested. Review proposed bulk changes before they are applied.

faq.question: Can it delete Linear records?
faq.answer: No deletion tools are listed in this skill.

faq.question: Can it create a new cycle?
faq.answer: The listed tools can read cycles, but they do not include a cycle creation tool.

faq.question: What happens when Linear MCP is unavailable?
faq.answer: The workflow pauses for connection and OAuth setup. Codex may require a restart after login.
